description.narrative: This project is a joint initiative by Royal LC Packaging International, Dutch-Bangla Pack Ltd., Woord en Daad, and the Father Charles Joseph Young Foundation, working together to improve social sustainability in the plastic waste and recycling value chain in and around Dhaka, Bangladesh. The focus lies on ensuring fair wages, safer working conditions, and more secure employment, particularly in the informal stages of the chain, such as waste picking, sorting, and collecting.The current value chain is largely informal, with workers, many of them women, youth, or from marginalised backgrounds, facing hazardous working environments, low pay, and limited access to labour rights or social protection. Despite increasing demand for recycled polypropylene (rPP), the early stages of the supply chain remain unregulated and underpaid.The project targets these upstream workers and small-scale operators as direct beneficiaries. By supporting more formal employment relationships and fairer compensation, the project also aims to benefit workers' families and communities indirectly. Special attention will be given to gender equity and the inclusion of disadvantaged groups.During Phase A, a local impact assessment will be conducted to understand root causes of labour-related risks and identify opportunities to structurally improve the value chain. Based on these insights, a co-created action plan will be developed for implementation in Phase B.The envisioned impact is the creation of a commercially viable and socially responsible PP recycling chain that aligns with international due diligence standards. It will enable participating companies to source recycled materials transparently and responsibly, while ensuring that workers benefit from dignified jobs, a safer work environment, and improved incomes, contributing to a circular economy that works for people as well as the planet.
